items.title: Tom Scott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 1, 2022 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: currently I think it’s called the Jim Hensen Studio now.

ctx.x: Okay. So let’s say we’re going to pick — you had mentioned 1973 that there was a heck of a lot of things you did that year. And in that time period can you talk me through a typical day in the life of Tom Scott as far as perhaps getting a call to play a solo on someone’s record. Can you tell me how that happens and then what it was like in the studio?

You bet, sure. First of all your job if you’re playing a solo on someone else’s record obviously your job is to provide a service. You’re a gun for hire so to speak and your job is to make them happy with whatever you do. So I look to the artist and/or the producer to give me any input that they want to. Sometimes it’s in musical terms, many times it isn’t. You know they want it to feel some more emotion here or in the case of Joni Mitchell she was a painter you know, and still is a painter. So she would say I…

my previous trips into A&M. So I get a call, “Carole King would like you to play on her record.” Okay, great. What instruments do I need? I need a tenor saxophone, okay, great. Because at the time you know I regularly was expected to have at my fingertips well my woodwind battery consisted of piccolo, flute, alto flute, bass flute, clarinet, bass clarinet, soprano — actually sopranino, soprano, alto, tenor, baritone and then recorders. I had a soprano recorder, a tenor recorder — yeah those two. So it was a lot…
